To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new approach to evaluate the spatio temporal distribution of societal risk to the population from landslides, which is based on the frequency distribution of fatal landslide events and the scaling exponent that controls the proportion of small and large magnitude fatal landslides; we used the approach to prepare a map of societal landslide risk for Italy, which is a complex function of the magnitude of the largest fatal landslide, of the number of fatal landslide events, and of the scaling exponent of fatal landslide frequency

we developed a novel approach to model societal landslide hazard and risk from historical, point information on the fatal consequences of landslides; that we applied this approach to Italy, and that the results show that the societal landslide risk in different parts of Italy is not uniform.

the Zipf model of landslide frequency is adequate to model societal landslide hazard and risk in Italy, and that the spatial distribution of societal landslide frequency, the number of fatal landslde events, and the scaling exponent in the Zipf distribution, are key variables to model landslide risk in Italy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

societal landslide risk in a specific geographical area, but it has the potential to contribute to the development of a more comprehensive and effective approach to model the societal risk of other natural and technological hazards, in Italy and in other countries.
the societal consequences of landslides, which is the ultimate goal of landslide research.
the spatial and temporal distribution of societal risk, and with the development and testing of a novel methodology that can be used to prepare and validate risk models for other types of hazards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach can be applied to model the spatial and temporal distribution of landslide risk, and of the risk caused by other natural and human induced hazards, for which adequate historical information is available.
the proposed methodology is an important step forward to model societal risk from landslides.
the approach is useful for modelling the societal consequences of landslides, but also for other hazards.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the face of the complexity and the uncertainty of landslide risk, we propose a simple and robust approach to model and communicate the risk to society.
, in the context of societal landslide risk, a single number cannot describe the spatial and temporal distribution of risk.
the approach is a new tool for landslide risk management, and that the approach can be applied to model the societal risk from other natural hazards.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Zipf law is a useful tool to describe the frequency of extreme events, and that it can be used to model the societal risk of rare events in a variety of contexts, from natural hazards to crime, and from finance to social sciences.
, in the absence of a comprehensive dataset on landslide fatalities, the Zipf distribution can be adopted to model societal landslide fatalities.
, despite the difficulty in modelling rare, sparse events, a predictive model of societal risk can be developed using a limited amount of data.
